A narrowing conversion loses information, e.g. 4.5 stored in an int becomes 4 (the fraction is dropped).

int x{ 4.5 };   list-init: required diagnostic (usually an error)
int x = 4.5;    copy-init: compiles, silently becomes 4
int x(4.5);     direct-init: compiles, silently becomes 4

Later assignment still allows narrowing: after a list-init, x = 4.5; is legal.
front: What is a narrowing conversion, and how do the initialization forms treat int x = 4.5 vs int x(4.5) vs int x{ 4.5 }?
